Let \(\alpha=\angle BAC\), \(\beta=\angle ABC\), \(\gamma=\angle ACB\). Then
\[
AB=r\left(\cot\frac\alpha2+\cot\frac\beta2\right),\qquad 
AC=r\left(\cot\frac\alpha2+\cot\frac\gamma2\right),\qquad 
CI=\frac{r}{\sin(\gamma/2)}.
\]
Using \(AB=AC+CI\):
\[
\cot\frac\beta2=\cot\frac\gamma2+\csc\frac\gamma2
=\frac{1+\cos(\gamma/2)}{\sin(\gamma/2)}
=\cot\frac\gamma4.
\]
Since \(0<\beta/2,\gamma/4<\pi/2\), we get
\[
\frac\beta2=\frac\gamma4 \implies 2\beta=\gamma.
\]
Therefore,
\[
\frac{\widehat{ACB}}{\widehat{ABC}}=\frac{\gamma}{\beta}=2.
\]

\[
\boxed{2}
\]
